title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has published its response to a report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards, outlining its stance and policies on AI. The document aims to address the recommendations made by the committee, providing a framework for the development and regulation of AI in public settings.

title: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) in education
description: The Department for Education’s (DfE) position on the use of generative AI in the education sector.
summary: This document outlines the UK Department for Education's view on using generative AI in schools. It likely discusses the potential benefits and limitations of using AI tools in educational settings.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: This document outlines Ofqual's approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector, providing a framework for its implementation and oversight. The policy aims to ensure AI is used responsibly and transparently in the awarding of qualifications.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines the relationship between copyright and artificial intelligence, focusing on how copyrighted works are used in AI development. It aims to assess the potential impact of AI on copyright laws and vice versa.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has responded to a report by the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence, acknowledging concerns and potential risks associated with AI. The government aims to address these issues and create regulations that ensure the safe and beneficial development of AI in the UK.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document outlines a set of guidelines and questions to be considered by a committee reviewing artificial intelligence in the context of public standards. It likely focuses on the social implications and appropriate regulations for AI within a public setting.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: The UK's Committee on Standards in Public Life (CSPL) has submitted evidence to a parliamentary inquiry on regulating AI, contributing to the discussion on how to govern artificial intelligence in the UK. This submission aims to inform the committee's recommendations for overseeing the development and use of AI.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This document discusses how artificial intelligence (AI) is affecting regulations around medical products, aiming to update existing laws and policies to accommodate AI technology. It involves implementing the recommendations from an AI White Paper, possibly to improve safety, efficiency, and quality in the medical industry.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The defence organisation aims to become the world's most effective and efficient Defence organisation in terms of artificial intelligence. This will make the organisation the most trusted and influential Defence entity globally in AI capabilities.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan is a government strategy to develop and utilize AI technology in the transport sector. It aims to balance the benefits of AI with potential risks in an effort to create a safe and efficient transportation system.
